narrative.overview:
The console wears Shoof's own identity: a deep burgundy rail, warm ivory paper for the work, espresso ink, and roasted terracotta for what is being spent. The home reads like a souk stall seen from across the lane: the menu laid out as open bins, each filled with its own dishes' photos to the level of its 3D readiness; the day's work hung as paper order tickets on a steel kitchen rail; a shelf of real dishes below. The colour on these surfaces comes from the food photography; the chrome stays ivory and sand.

The density is an operator's density: one hairline-ruled ledger slab instead of a band of equal cards, big tabular numerals with quiet labels, sand hairlines instead of boxes inside boxes. Arabic is the first language and the layout mirrors in RTL; IBM Plex Sans Arabic with IBM Plex Sans (self-hosted) carries both scripts. Material lives in the signature objects (bins, tickets, the rail's clip and bar, the dish photos), not in textures painted onto every surface.

Sign-in is "the dish and the eye": always the light set, an espresso stage with a drifting wall of real dish photos washed in burgundy, a plate holding a turning dish beside the watching eye of the Shoof mark, and an ivory form column carrying the official logo.
keyCharacteristics: Burgundy rail with a slight top-light depth; the active page is an ivory pill with burgundy text.
Ivory ground and paper cards; real dish photography is the colour.
Terracotta means spent (quota and usage); plain progress is burgundy (sand in dark); red is only for failure.
One 76px readiness figure per home; every other figure is a 28px tabular numeral.
Category bins, kitchen tickets and a dish shelf are the home's signature objects.
Sign-in is always the daylight (light) set.

rules.name: The Logo Keeps Its Colours Rule
rules.body: The Shoof mark is always a burgundy tile with ivory plates, in every theme and on every surface. The tile-less mark and wordmark use burgundy on light and ivory on dark. The console's own palette never re-themes the logo.

rules.name: The Terracotta Is Spent Rule
rules.body: A terracotta meter is a quota being consumed; plain progress (readiness, tables with QR, active dishes, plan period) is a burgundy meter, sand in dark. In light mode terracotta is never a button fill.

rules.name: The Red Means Failure Rule
rules.body: Destructive red marks only failed jobs, the hot ticket and a quota that is used up. Everything else that needs attention stays in espresso ink with an icon.

rules.name: The Photography Is The Colour Rule
rules.body: On the home and the menu, colour comes from the restaurant's own dish photos; surfaces around them stay ivory, sand and espresso. A missing photo shows the bin colour with a faint burgundy diagonal hatch and a "no photo" note, never a stock image.

rules.name: The Section Hue Rule
rules.body: Each navigation section owns one hue (terracotta Menu, ochre AI, rose Restaurant, slate Team), used only on that section's head icon on the rail. It is not a fill anywhere.

rules.name: The One Hero Figure Rule
rules.body: The readiness percentage is the page's only hero figure. No other figure on the home repeats it or competes with its size.

rules.name: The Quiet Label Rule
rules.body: A figure is set large and tabular; its label is 0.75rem muted ink and never competes with it. A share always says what it is a share of ("20 of 51").

rules.name: The Lining Numerals Rule
rules.body: All numerals are lining and tabular in figures and tables; the UI's own numerals are used (Arabic-Indic in Arabic). Numbers in mixed-direction strings are isolated LTR.

rules.name: The Hairline Ledger Rule
rules.body: Values that belong together sit in one slab, divided by sand hairlines (cells overlap by -1px so rules never double), never by nested cards or tiles.

rules.name: The Objects Carry Depth Rule
rules.body: Cards are flat paper. Only the things on the display (bins, tickets, the rail, the active pill) are lifted. The rail's top-light gradient is the one gradient that stands in for light.

dos: Do use the single motion curve `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for entrances, fills, rolling digits and the nav pill; interface feedback always animates, decorative loops stop under reduced motion, and a still frame always shows the final state.
Do draw every share with the one meter, saying what it is a share of.
Do keep terracotta for spending and marks, burgundy for actions and plain progress.
Do let dish photos carry the colour on the home and menu, and show the hatched bin when a photo is missing.
Do name the work on an attention ticket and link straight to where it is fixed.
Do mirror layouts with logical properties (start/end) so Arabic and English share one layout.
donts: Don't set the home as a band of equal cards, or nest cards inside the ledger slab.
Don't use terracotta as a light-mode button fill or for plain progress.
Don't use red for anything but failure, the hot ticket and a used-up quota.
Don't repeat or rival the readiness figure elsewhere on the home.
Don't put small uppercase labels above headings; the date and restaurant name follow the greeting.
